figs.title: Unconstrained and constrained minimum of one function
figs.caption: Solve the unconstrained problem first. When its minimizer violates a constraint, the constrained minimum lies on that boundary, where a contour of f is tangent to g = 0 and ∇f = −μ∇g with μ > 0.

figs.title: Linear, superlinear and quadratic convergence
figs.caption: On a log error axis steepest descent falls along a straight line (linear rate), BFGS bends downward (superlinear), and Newton drops ever faster as the correct digits double each iteration (quadratic). The curves come from running each method on the same convex function from the same start.

figs.caption: Samples and basis functions build Φ with Φᵢⱼ = φⱼ(xᵢ), and the weights minimize the squared error, giving ΦᵀΦw = Φᵀy. The shape of Φ sets the case: square interpolates, tall regresses, wide needs the minimum norm solution or ridge.

figs.title: Kriging uncertainty and expected improvement
figs.caption: Kriging gives a mean prediction and a standard error s(x) that is zero at the samples and grows between them. Expected improvement rewards both a low mean and a large s, and its maximum picks the next sample in efficient global optimization.

figs.title: Quadratic penalty path as ρ grows
figs.caption: Each quadratic penalty minimizer x(ρ) lies outside the feasible set and approaches x* as ρ increases. The product ρ·g(x(ρ)) estimates the multiplier and converges to μ*.

figs.title: Active set strategy loop
figs.caption: Guess a working set from physical reasoning, solve with those constraints as equalities, then add any violated constraint and drop any constraint with a negative multiplier. The loop ends at a feasible point with every μ ≥ 0, which is a KKT point.
